purpose: Test the existing author SAMURAI video tracker on seq11, seq20 and seq23 using the exact one-time original-YOLO-derived mask used by the verified automatic Lean run. Historical SAMURAI used a ground-truth prompt and is not a matched automatic control.
inputs: Reuse the archived verified automatic prompt mask and its original detection frame. No new detector call or redetection. For seq23, use the exact fixed inset-excluded viewport and restore masks to full coordinates. Preserve original source-frame IDs when rebasing SAMURAI to its required frame-zero prompt. Frames before initialization are empty, as in the automatic Lean run.
verification: Inspect the pinned SAMURAI author checkpoint and CPU rotary behavior; test prompt-mask and viewport geometry, frame rebase and full-resolution restoration. Require a short repeated label-free inference check and exact model identity before any full run. Freeze all predictions and hashes before opening labels; independently rescore. Compare same source-frame IDs, present Dice and empty-frame false alarms against existing automatic Lean reference without rerunning it. Include all three difficult sequences and preserve all receipts under Google Drive outputs/experiment.
limitations: SAMURAI changes the whole tracking system and author memory behavior. Even with identical prompts and target frames, different implementations and temporal memory prevent attributing effects to one token mechanism. Existing sequences are retrospective, patient independence and original detector exposure are unknown, and annotations may be incomplete. Do not add a confidence gate, new threshold or redetection. Do not claim improvement without measured outcomes.
